findings.summary: the compose sweep's blanket `catch` would have swallowed this port's OWN contract errors, not just the pin's inapplicable-arm refusal — and the same branch adds two new throw sites inside `composePinnedPbrVariant`, so a material whose other thirty-one arms died of a port defect would have reported `ok`. Only the pin's refusal is skipped now: `topoSort` throws a bare `Error()` with no message and every refusal this port raises carries one, so the message is the discriminator and anything with one re-throws

the prelude inventory guard was blind in the direction a bump actually moves: nothing enumerated `_buildShapeParams`'s case clauses or the `params.<property>` assignments inside them, so a case the pin adds — or a parameter it starts deriving inside an existing one, which is exactly what 1.25.0 did to the capsule and the cylinder — was silently dropped against whatever the emitted shape hardcodes (the box's identity rotation is the standing example). `assertShapeParamsCases` enumerates both

the composer's key-set check used SET EQUALITY, which refuses a purely additive optional dependency — `PbrComposerDeps._tm` is already optional. The rule is every supplied key declared, and every REQUIRED declared key supplied

the same untyped-bag hazard sits on the second such bag in the tree with no check at all: `pinned-node-material.ts` hands `compileNodePipeline` an eleven-key literal against the pin's thirteen-member `CompileOpts`, where a renamed `_esmShadowDepthCode` would compose an ESM caster with no depth code. Checked by the same helper

`assertComposerDependencies` read pinned AST outside `LoweringContext` — `sharedUpstreamStore().getSourceFile()` directly, its own member-name read where `propertyName` handles the string and numeric member names an interface can legally carry, and two bare `throw`s where `contractError` carries `file:line:col`. It is `LoweringContext.assertSuppliedOptions` now, beside a new `interfaceDeclaration` peer to `functionDeclaration`

the new module-scope-constant scan did not test `NodeFlags.Const`, where the sibling it most resembles does — and the very module the rule first reached is the demonstration: `hdr-ibl-pipeline.ts` declares `HDR_LOD_GENERATION_SCALE` on one line and a mutable `let _prefilteredEnvironmentExtraUsage = 0` counter the pin means to change on the next. Without the flag test a reader would bake the counter's initial value into generated C++ with no contract error

that scan was a third copy of one walk. It is `LoweringContext.moduleScopeConstant` now, and three callers took it: `pinned-shader-text.ts`'s private copy (keeping its deliberate refusal to follow an import), `PhysicsLowerer.maxStepMs` and `standardPluginConstant`, both of which had been reaching it through the whole-subtree `variableInitializer`. Proved byte-exact: `compile all` moves ZERO generated files against a post-sweep baseline (1700 `.slots` prune aside, which only `process` republishes)

the physics lowerer was the only one of twelve `PinnedNumericLowerer` consumers not seeding its `Math.*` table from the shared `pinnedNumericMathCalls()` — its `Math.abs` entry was a verbatim duplicate of the shared spelling, and a `Math.min` or `Math.sqrt` the pin added to `_buildShapeParams` would have refused here while working in the other eleven. It seeds from the table and layers only `Math.max`, which the pin calls with three arguments where the shared spelling is the two-argument form

the three `extents.{x,y,z}` bindings were dead — the `vec3` binding one line above resolves a member access to the identical text, proven by an A/B that left `source` and `header` byte-identical. Deleted; the block read as symmetric with the `node.scaling.${axis}` one above it, where only that one carries the double widening

each prelude scalar's (pinned name, emitted field) pairing was stated three times and its pinned name a fourth, with nothing checking the pairings agree — binding `scaleY` while assigning from `scaleYMagnitude` would have passed every check and shipped the wrong scale. One `PRELUDE_SCALARS` table now derives the bindings, the struct fields, the assignments and half the inventory

`capsule_shape` and `cylinder_shape` were the same eight-line emission written twice, with the capsule's local hoisted out as a one-off. One `segment(caseName)` closure emits both and reads each case's own locals, so a pin that gives the cylinder one works instead of needing a second hoist

`assertShapeParamsPrelude` and `assertStepWorldInventory` were one helper written twice 300 lines apart — same shape, same refusal wording. One `assertInventory` taking the projection as a parameter serves both, and the next pinned body this port restates whole

four hand-rolled `?? ` splits in one file, each with its own spelling of the same two tests. They go through `LoweringContext.nullishDefault`; `coalescedPropertyDefault` in the glTF lowerers stays as the specialization that additionally names the property on the left, which the physics defaults do not have (`gravity ?? {...}` is a bare parameter)

`boundVector(name, member)` took a second parameter fully determined by the first, so `("min", "maximum")` would have emitted a builder filling `shape.minimum` from `box.maximum` and passed every check in the file. Derived from the name

`pinnedToneMapping` re-listed the record's three fields at its exit, in the same change whose comment says the record is carried whole — a field the pin adds next bump would be dropped by exactly the mechanism that dropped the composer's tone mapping. It returns the record
`composable` was an int counter only ever compared `=== 0`, inviting a reader to look for a use of the count that does not exist. A boolean

efficiency angle: measured, nothing to fix. `assertSuppliedOptions` re-parses nothing (the store memoizes source files) at 1.55 us/call against 336 calls for a fourteen-material scene; `lowerShapeParams` walks the switch AST eleven times at 13 ms cold for a function called once per scene before a C++ compile; the new identifier branch in `numericValue` runs only where the old code was about to throw. The one measurable new cost is ~0.9 s of test-suite time from three test files that now build the upstream store transitively
findings.blockedBy: nothing — there is no defect here to fix; recorded so the next review does not re-derive the measurements

findings.summary: the deeper form of the compose-sweep fix would filter the candidate list per subject — a transmissive material composes only under the `+ibl` arms, which `sceneCandidates()` could tag and `materialSubjects` already knows — so no throw would be expected at all
findings.blockedBy: it encodes 'transmissive implies ibl' as a rule THIS port states, where the message discriminator keeps the pin's own `refraction -> ibl` dependency as the authority; a second fragment pair with the same shape would need the rule extended here rather than being answered by the pin
findings.filedIn: not filed: the applied form covers the hazard the finding named (a port defect reported as `ok`), and the residual is a preference rather than an unfinished job

findings.summary: `PinnedNumericLowerer.moduleConstant` is a fourth copy of the module-scope-constant walk and could take the shared scan
findings.blockedBy: it is a different contract wearing the same shape: it returns a lowered `PinnedBinding` rather than an initializer, memoizes through a self-reference guard, and takes the LAST match where the shared scan takes the first. Switching it is a behaviour change on a path fifteen lowerers reach, with no measurement in this branch that would catch it
findings.filedIn: TODO.md is not the right home for it — the shared scan is in place and this copy's divergence is documented at its own declaration; a third caller wanting a lowered constant is what would justify merging them
